MGR-native multi-view silhouette reconstruction (space carving).

This module turns *measured* orthographic silhouettes into real triangle
geometry. It is deliberately honest about what it can and cannot know:

- Occupancy is constrained by every supplied silhouette at once.
- Concavities and surfaces no view can see are **not** measured; they are
  bounded by the visual hull, never invented.
- No neural model, no external API, no GPU is involved.

Coordinate convention: Y is up, X is width, Z is depth. Front/back views look
along -Z/+Z, so image X maps to world X. Left/right views look along +X/-X, so
image X maps to world Z. Image Y always maps to world Y with the top row at the
top of the bounds.

Back and right cameras sit on the far side of the subject, so their masks are
mirrored horizontally before carving. Supply each mask exactly as that camera
sees it; an unmirrored back/right mask makes the supplied silhouettes
contradict each other and the fit gate fails loudly instead of guessing.

Optional SAM (Segment Anything) adapter behind the F108 contract.

This module is **import-safe**: if torch / segment_anything are not installed in
the running interpreter it still imports and `SamAdapter.available()` returns
False *unless* a Python 3.12 worker with torch + weights is available, in which
case segmentation is delegated to `scripts/sam_segment.py`.

SAM is free (Apache 2.0) but heavy: PyTorch + model weights (~375 MB for
ViT-B, ~2.4 GB for ViT-H) and a GPU is strongly recommended. On CPU it works
but is slow (seconds to tens of seconds per image).

Honest scope of what this adapter does today:
- `mode="center"` : segment the subject around the image centre (useful for
  isolating a character from a clean reference).
- `mode="auto"`    : run SAM's automatic mask generator and return the largest
  mask (useful for exploration; not part-level).
Full part-level segmentation (hair/face/body/clothing) is NOT implemented:
it requires prompted masks or a downstream classifier and is open work.
